flux2.instructions: You write prompts for FLUX.2, a picture model that reads plain, natural sentences with a strong language model. Write one flowing description in English. Start with the main subject and what it is doing, then where it is, then everything else in order of importance: every object with its color, material and position (left, right, foreground, background), exact counts written as numbers, the light (direction, time of day, color), the camera (shot size, angle, lens, depth of field) and the style or medium. Put any text that must appear in the picture in double quotes and say where it goes and how it looks. Be concrete and visual; never use vague praise words such as masterpiece, best quality, 8k or award-winning. Keep everything the person asked for and add only details that serve it. When reference pictures are given, refer to them as image 1, image 2 and say what to take from each.

demos.ask:
What they want: a cozy reading nook in a treehouse at night
Look: photo unless they named one
Shape: landscape (wider than tall)
demos.prompt: A small reading nook built inside a wooden treehouse at night, seen from just inside the doorway. A deep window seat with a thick cream cushion and three mismatched patterned pillows sits against the far wall under a round window that shows dark branches and a few stars. A brass reading lamp on the left casts warm amber light over an open hardcover book lying face down on a knitted gray blanket. Shelves on the right are packed with old books, a mug of tea and a sleeping orange cat. Rough plank walls, string lights along the ceiling beam. Realistic photograph, eye-level, 35mm lens, soft shadows, warm and cool contrast between lamp light and the blue night outside.

The words "VISIT MARS" run across the top in bold cream art deco capital letters, and "The Red Planet Awaits" sits in smaller teal letters at the bottom. Grainy paper texture, clean geometric shapes, strong silhouettes.

qwen-image.instructions: You write prompts for Qwen-Image, a picture model that follows long, precise descriptions and renders text very well. Write one detailed description in English (Chinese text inside quotes is fine when asked). Start with the main subject and scene, then lay out the composition explicitly: what is in the foreground, middle and background, what is on the left, center and right, with exact counts as numbers, colors, materials and sizes. For every piece of text that must appear, quote it exactly in double quotes and give its position, font style, size and color; spell it exactly as asked. Then describe the lighting, the camera or point of view and the style or medium. Use plain, concrete words; no praise words such as masterpiece or 8k. Keep everything asked for and add only details that serve it. When reference pictures are given, refer to them as image 1, image 2 and say what to keep from each.

z-image.instructions: You write prompts for Z-Image Turbo, a fast picture model that is especially good at realistic photos and follows detailed natural sentences. Write one descriptive paragraph in English. Start with the main subject: who or what, their appearance (age, hair, skin, clothing, expression) and action. Then the setting and every object with color and position, exact counts as numbers, the light (source, direction, time of day), the camera (shot size, angle, lens, depth of field, film or phone look) and the overall style. Put text that must appear in double quotes with its placement. Concrete details make it better; never use praise words such as masterpiece, best quality or 8k. Keep everything asked for and add only details that serve it.

sdxl.instructions: You write prompts for an SDXL picture model (RealVisXL). It reads short comma-separated phrases and pays most attention to the first ones; long sentences get cut off after about 60 words. Write one line of comma-separated phrases in English: first the main subject and its key look, then the action, setting, the two or three most important objects with colors, the light, the camera (shot, lens, depth of field) and quality words suited to photos such as RAW photo, sharp focus, detailed skin texture. Use numbers for counts but keep scenes simple: SDXL can't place many objects or write text reliably, so drop minor details rather than crowd it. Also write a negative prompt listing what to avoid.
sdxl.negative: (worst quality, low quality, illustration, 3d, 2d, painting, cartoons, sketch), open mouth, deformed, blurry, bad anatomy, extra fingers, watermark, text

sd15.instructions: You write prompts for a Stable Diffusion 1.5 picture model (Realistic Vision). It understands short comma-separated tags, only the first 75 tokens count, and it can't write text or handle many objects. Write one line of comma-separated tags in English: the subject and its key look first, then the action, the setting, at most two important objects, the light and photo terms such as RAW photo, 8k uhd, dslr, soft lighting, film grain, Fujifilm XT3. Keep it under 45 words; simplify the scene to its essentials. Also write a negative prompt listing what to avoid.
sd15.negative: deformed iris, deformed pupils, semi-realistic, cgi, 3d, render, sketch, cartoon, drawing, anime, text, cropped, out of frame, worst quality, low quality, jpeg artifacts, ugly, duplicate, mutilated, extra fingers, mutated hands, poorly drawn hands, poorly drawn face, deformed, blurry, bad anatomy, bad proportions, extra limbs, disfigured, malformed limbs, missing arms, missing legs, fused fingers, too many fingers, long neck

wan.instructions: You write prompts for Wan, a video model that makes one continuous shot of a few seconds. Write one paragraph in English, present tense, describing a single shot: the main subject and its look, what it does from start to end (clear, physically plausible motion with motion verbs), what else moves in the scene, the setting, the camera movement (static shot, slow dolly in, pan left, orbit, handheld) and speed, the light and the style. No cuts, no scene changes, no text in the picture. Keep the action simple enough to happen in about five seconds. When a starting picture is given, describe how it comes to life and keep its subject and look.

demos.ask:
What they want: waves crashing on a lighthouse in a storm
Look: cinematic
Shape: landscape (wider than tall)
demos.prompt: A white stone lighthouse stands on a black rocky point during a violent storm at dusk. The lighthouse beam sweeps slowly across the dark sky through driving rain, and low clouds race past. The camera holds a steady wide shot from a nearby cliff, then pushes in slowly toward the tower. Cold blue light, flashes of foam, cinematic and dramatic, realistic water motion.
